parallel.requirements: Recognized the C++ program as parsing optional n with default 5, pushing 0..n into an immutable vector, printing size, using std-only Rust, and placing test1.rs in /output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although swarm mode was injected, the main actor decided the task was too small for delegation and kept implementation, verification, and delivery ownership locally.
parallel.implementation: Created persistent_vector.rs with a clone-on-push Vector<T> wrapper and test1.rs that parses args, builds the vector, and prints v.len().
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated the module through mod persistent_vector in test1.rs, compiled with rustc to /output/test1, and left the expected entry file and module in the artifact.
parallel.verification: Ran rustc and compared outputs with the C++ executable for no arg, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, and 100; all local checks passed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed 5 of 38 tests. The raw trajectory does not expose the exact failing cases; likely gaps are ordinary semantic edge cases rather than coordination failures.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same optional n/default-5 behavior, persistent-vector semantics, stdout format, std-only constraint, root test1.rs, and module organization requirement.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single main actor owned implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery without delegation or child-agent activity.
serial.implementation: Created immer.rs with a clone-on-push Vector<T> wrapper and test1.rs that parses args, builds the vector, and prints v.size().
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated the module through mod immer in test1.rs, compiled with rustc to /output/test1, and left test1.rs plus immer.rs in the artifact.
serial.verification: Ran rustc and compared outputs with the C++ executable for 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, -3, and no-argument default; all local checks passed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed 5 of 38 tests. The raw trajectory does not expose the exact failing cases; the serial code made a similar simple parser choice as parallel.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are concordant failures: both parallel and serial scored 33/38 and solution_passed false. The trajectories produced near-equivalent direct implementations and both passed small local reference comparisons before closure. Because the parallel run did not execute any child-agent or multi-agent mechanism, there is no parallel-side coordination episode that can explain the shared official shortfall.
parallel_contributors: Parallel made a direct no-delegation implementation despite swarm mode and delivered a simple clone-on-push vector plus parse().expect entry point.
serial_contributors: Serial made a direct implementation with the same simple parser/vector strategy and one additional negative-argument local check.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The helper module name and exposed length method differ: persistent_vector::Vector::len in parallel versus immer::Vector::size in serial.
Both solutions likely share the same ordinary edge-case limitations that caused five official failures, but the exact failing cases are not present in the mounted pair evidence.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference and no qualifying parallel mechanism
